88778362.title: File:20200314 - The Korea Times - Wuhan coronavirus - Are Koreans really scared.webm

ImageDescription.value: The deadly coronavirus epidemic that originated in Wuhan, China, has been dominating headlines around the world. And media coverage in neighboring South Korea has been inflammatory, fueling public fear over the virus. The Korea Times reporters visited Myeongdong which was far less densely populated with Chinese tourists  than right before the coronavirus outbreak and asked people in the streets how they feel about the epidemic. Business owners and employees working in Myeongdong were reluctant to speak to the press about the virus, fearing it could further affect their sales.

171941298.title: File:강남역 江南驛 Gangnam Station, Seoul.png

ImageDescription.value:
Gangnam Station is located in the heart of Seoul, the capital of South Korea, right at the center of its most vibrant commercial district. Renowned as a global hub for medical beauty, the area boasts one of the highest concentrations of plastic surgery and dermatology clinics in the world — a name that any foreign visitor interested in Korean beauty has likely heard before. Nearly every floor of the surrounding buildings is home to a clinic, attracting a steady flow of international medical tourists seeking state-of-the-art equipment, advanced surgical techniques, and a wide range of beauty programs. Gangnam Station has firmly established itself as a global beauty mecca, offering foreign visitors the perfect place to experience the cutting edge of Korea’s beauty industry firsthand.

Transportation is another key advantage of Gangnam Station. Known as a true “transportation mecca” in the very heart of Seoul, it serves as a major transfer point where Subway Line 2 and the Shinbundang Line intersect. This allows foreign travelers to move easily between the city’s main tourist attractions and business districts, while also connecting quickly to southern Gyeonggi areas such as Bundang, Pangyo, and Suwon. The Shinbundang Line provides direct or minimal-transfer access to Yeouido, Gwanghwamun, Myeongdong, and even Incheon and Gimpo International Airports. The bus network around the station is equally extensive. Major city, express, night, and airport limousine buses run along Gangnam-daero, linking Gangnam to all parts of Seoul, surrounding metropolitan cities, and airports in under an hour. With designated taxi stands, ride-hailing services, and even public bike rentals, first-time visitors to Seoul enjoy complete freedom to travel anywhere, anytime — without the stress of navigating a large, complex city.

Infrastructure around Gangnam Station is exceptional. A vast underground shopping mall stretches beneath the station, offering fashion, beauty, and lifestyle goods, while above ground you’ll find large shopping malls, department stores, cinemas, premium cafés, and restaurants. In just one day, foreign visitors can shop, dine, receive medical treatment, and enjoy leisure activities all within the same area. These combined features make Gangnam Station one of the must-visit destinations in South Korea.
